run: T0b: tail precision at equal accuracy
plain: Does a pairing (PP) network trained to the same overall accuracy as the ViT get the rare configurations more precisely? Compares six existing networks; no training
result: No: at equal overall accuracy the pairing networks are no more precise on rare configurations than the ViT (1.3x worse). Precision on rare configurations tracks overall accuracy, so the T0 kill stands

run: T0: pairing networks on rare configurations
plain: Fixed node with the corrected sign, using amplitude ratios from PP and RBM+PP networks instead of the ViT; measures the error on rare configurations
result: Kill rule fires: PP's rare-configuration error is 0.78x the ViT's (bar: 2x better). Every network gives about 0.8x its own variational error

run: ViT refit after the flip (2 seeds)
plain: Retrain the ViT to the best amplitudes for the corrected sign, then run fixed node with it
result: Fails: 9.2e-5 (bar 1e-5). Good down to probability 1e-9; configurations rarer than 1e-11 carry 60% of the error. Flip labels from the network find almost none of the wrong signs

plain: Fixed node with the best bond numbers: does the switched-off set hold the wrong signs, and does flipping it lower the energy?
result: Yes: switched-off set holds ~100% wrong signs by weight; flipping lowers the best energy 2.5e-6 to 9.1e-7

plain: Network predicts the bond numbers, trained on the fixed-node energy
result: Plateau 1.9e-5 (bar 1e-5): fails; also needs ~23 extra neighbour evaluations per step

plain: How expensive is training a 12x12 starting network (RBM+PP)?
result: 97 s per step; at least 266 H100-h (bar 100): too expensive as configured

plain: Formal analysis of fixed node with free bond numbers, flip rule, scaling
result: Exact flip rule found; loop can only settle on the ground state

plain: Conceptual check of the bond-number idea
result: Best bond numbers mostly switch off wrong-sign configurations
